blogTitle: How Do I Visualize My Gallery Wall Before Installing?
videoTitle: How Do I Visualize My Gallery Wall Before Installing?
script:
How Do I Visualize My Gallery Wall Before Installing?

Okay — have you ever stood in front of a blank wall, hammer in hand, and just… frozen? [warmly] That moment of panic is EXACTLY why we plan before we hang.

Here's the thing — there are three core methods for visualising your gallery wall before a single nail goes in… digital apps, paper templates, and painter's tape outlines, right?

Before you open ANY app or cut a single piece of paper — measure your wall FIRST, with a proper steel tape measure, not a fabric one.

On your wall map, record the full width and height — but also mark EVERY obstacle… sockets, switches, radiators, windows. Trust me, I've seen gorgeous layouts ruined by a forgotten plug socket.

[excited] And the good news? You can plan your whole layout digitally — for FREE — using tools like Canva or a dedicated gallery wall planner, before you touch your walls at all.

There are paid tools with more features, but honestly… free apps get the job done beautifully for most people. A little tip I love: start with a free tier, see if you need more.

On your phone, apps like Canva make this really simple — you just set your canvas to your wall dimensions and drag frame shapes around until everything CLICKS.

Quick walkthrough for Canva on your phone — open a custom canvas, type in your wall measurements, then drop in rectangles for each frame size… move them around, it's genuinely satisfying.

Now — the paper template method… cut newspaper or kraft paper to the EXACT outer size of each frame, label them, and tape them straight onto the wall with painter's tape.

[sighs] No app alone catches everything — and no paper method shows you the full picture before you commit. So honestly? I always recommend doing BOTH… digital first, then paper to confirm.

If you want a head start, you can use a printable gallery wall planning template — just print it, sketch your wall dimensions on it, and start mapping your frames by hand.

To make your own template, just list all your frames with their OUTER dimensions — the most common standard sizes are A4, A3, 50x70cm, and 30x40cm… those four cover most gallery walls.

When it comes to spacing — keep gaps between frames consistent, usually 5 to 8 centimetres… and choose your frames BEFORE you commit to holes, not after.

Here's a set I genuinely love for a gallery wall — the Japanese Dragons set of three. [warmly] The tonal, muted detail means they anchor a whole arrangement without competing with each other.

The most common planning mistakes? Forgetting wall obstacles, measuring the print instead of the FRAME outer size, and skipping the paper check before drilling. All so easy to avoid.

And this black and white set of two is just EFFORTLESS for a gallery wall — clean lines, no fuss, works with almost any spacing or frame style you choose.

Before you hang ANYTHING — run through your pre-hanging checklist: wall map done, templates confirmed on the wall, hanging positions marked, spirit level to hand. That order matters.

If you've got a Japanese Sunset set of three — these black and white prints are perfect for smaller walls… they read as one cohesive piece but give you all the flexibility of three separate frames.

[curious] Now — does the room SIZE change how you plan? Yes, actually… on a narrow wall, go vertical and tighter. On a wide wall, anchor from the centre outward. The wall tells you the rhythm.

For a New York-inspired living room wall, this set of three in white and black is honestly one of my favourites — that graphic, urban energy balances perfectly with a minimal frame arrangement.

There are so many gallery wall STYLES to explore — symmetrical grids, organic salon-style, all-same-frame, or mixed shapes… the style you pick should feel like YOU, not just what's trending.

This Art Living Room set of three has that calm, considered quality that just WORKS across so many gallery wall styles — classic tones, flexible sizing, easy to anchor a whole wall around.

[gently] One last thing before you hang — step back, look at your paper templates on the wall from across the room, and sit with it for a DAY if you can. Fresh eyes catch things a measuring tape never will.

The Zen Art set of three — soft, meditative, beautifully tonal — this is the kind of wall art that actually makes a room feel CALMER the moment you look at it.

And if you want something with real visual depth — this Modern Asian Inspired set of three has that layered, considered quality that makes a gallery wall feel genuinely CURATED rather than just filled.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

We've built a free set of Home Decor tools and styling guides…

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
